messages.subject: [RQt-devel] Crash with qrepl()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I just started looking into this project. I have an R package that
currently does some GUI stuff with RGtk2, and in my development
version I am switching to tcltk, but at some point down the line, I
would like to use Qt.

I found one crash with qrepl() that seems to be different from the
crashes you have been discussing the last couple of days. If you just
call qrepl(), input a line of R code into the widget, and press
Control-Return to execute it, you get the crash below.

Thanks,
Ben Goodrich

> library(qtutils); qrepl()
Loading required package: qtbase
Cannot handle Moc type 'qreal'

>
 *** caught segfault ***
address 0x4, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: .Call(qt_qenums, x)
 2: qenums(cl)
 3: qsmokeClass(lib, className)
 4: function () {    class <- qsmokeClass(lib, className)    rm(list =
className, envir = lib)    assign(className, class, lib)
lockBinding(className, lib)    class}()
 5: qinvoke(<environment>, "moveCursor", ...)
 6: outed$moveCursor(Qt$QTextCursor$End)
 7: executeCode(ined1$plainText, mode = "input")
 8: function (checked) {    executeCode(ined1$plainText, mode = "input")}()

Possible actions:
1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
2: normal R exit
3: exit R without saving workspace
4: exit R saving workspace

Sorry, replied to Justin instead of list ...


---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Ben Goodrich <bgokgm at googlemail.com>
Date: Wed, Dec 2, 2009 at 2:44 PM
Subject: Re: [RQt-devel] Crash with qrepl()
To: Justin Talbot <justintalbot at gmail.com>


Hi,

>>> Just wondering, why did you decide to move to tcltk?

RGtk2 and gWidgetsRGtk2 worked well for my own use, but the extra
installation steps of the Gtk2 library were causing headaches for
other people. For someone who installs R from the standard Mac or
Windows binaries, ?my package would install the standard way if I rely
on tcltk and gWidgetstcltk.

But now I might just revert to RGtk2 and wait until qtgui is ready to
go on CRAN. I guess people will still have to install the Qt library
separately, but hopefully I can improve my GUI enough to justify it. I
especially like QWizard and the potential to have a nice integrated
help system. The R help system is not ideal when users have a question
about an option the GUI gives them.

>> P.S.: Ben, I had to manually approve your mail as you are a
>> non-member. I've added you to the "approved senders" list, but also
>> consider subscribing to the list.

I subscribed right before I sent the original mail, but maybe it takes
a little while for it to register me.

> I can't reproduce this crash.

I just reinstalled all the packages from the svn sources and now it is
not crashing anymore. Previously, I had just done

install.packages(c("qtdevice", "qtpaint", "mosaiq"),
? ? ? ? ? ? ? ? repos = "http://r-forge.r-project.org")

I am not sure why that would make a difference if R-Forge builds the
packages daily from the trunk. But anyway, this crash is gone.

Thanks,
Ben
